docs.title: NetBox Cable Patcher
docs.text:
A visual patch bay interface for NetBox. Drag devices onto a canvas, see their ports laid out side-by-side, and create or remove cables by clicking between ports — no more hunting through forms to figure out what's plugged into what.

  • Free software: Apache-2.0
  • Documentation: https://joeladria.github.io/netbox-cable-patcher/
  • Source: https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Visual patch bay canvas: devices are shown as cards with ports along the facing edges, and cables are drawn as SVG bezier curves between connected ports.
  • Three dedicated modes — Network (interfaces, front/rear ports), Power (power ports/outlets), and Console (console ports/console server ports) — each with their own compatibility rules for what can be cabled together.
  • Click-to-patch: click an available port, then click a compatible port on another device to create a cable; click an existing cable to select it, inspect its details, and delete it (single or multi-select).
  • Create and delete cables directly from the canvas — changes are reflected instantly in the UI without a full page or data refresh.
  • Front port and rear port support, including patch-through connections.
  • Module bay visualization: device cards show module bays as outlined sections with the installed module type, and modules can be installed or uninstalled directly from the UI via a searchable module type picker.
  • Site / Location / Rack cascading filters (AJAX, no page reload); Location and Rack support selecting multiple values at once.
  • Cable defaults bar for setting type, color, and label before patching, plus a quick-patch toggle to skip the create-cable dialog.
  • Color-coded cables by type and status (e.g. planned, decommissioning).
  • Device drag-to-reorder within each column.
  • URL state persistence for site, location, rack, mode, and device selections, so a patch bay layout can be bookmarked or shared.
  • Keyboard shortcuts (Escape, Delete, Enter) and hover tooltips showing port type and connection status.
  • Dark mode support.
  • Permission-based access control for cable and module operations, backed by NetBox's own object permissions.
  • Cables created or deleted through the patcher record a distinct changelog message ("Modified by Cable Patcher Plugin") so they're easy to tell apart from changes made elsewhere in NetBox.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: NetBox Version Plugin Version 4.5 0.4.2 4.0 0.1.0

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
For adding to a NetBox Docker setup see the general instructions for using netbox-docker with plugins.

Install from PyPI:

pip install netbox-cable-patcher

or install the latest development version directly from GitHub:

pip install git+https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher

or by adding to your local_requirements.txt or plugin_requirements.txt (netbox-docker):

netbox-cable-patcher

Enable the plugin in /opt/netbox/netbox/netbox/configuration.py, or if you use netbox-docker, your /configuration/plugins.py file :

PLUGINS = [
    'netbox_cable_patcher'
]

PLUGINS_CONFIG = {
    "netbox_cable_patcher": {},
}

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
Created and maintained by Joel Adria and Moment Factory.

Based on the NetBox plugin tutorial:

  • demo repository
  • tutorial

This package was created with Cookiecutter and the netbox-community/cookiecutter-netbox-plugin project template.

• Updated project metadata: authors are now Joel Adria and Moment Factory; minimum supported Python is now 3.13 (was 3.10); minimum supported NetBox version is now 4.5.0 (was 4.0.0).
  • Fixed placeholder/broken GitHub URLs (repo, issues, discussions, documentation) across README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, pyproject.toml, mkdocs.yml, and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml to point to https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher.
  • Rewrote the README feature list and compatibility table to reflect the actual functionality shipped through v0.4.2, and updated the credits section.

• Port connect/disconnect state (cable line, port color/icon, connected badge in hover tooltip) now updates instantly after creating or deleting a cable by patching the affected ports' cable_id/connected_endpoint directly in local state, instead of refetching all devices and cables from the server.

• Fixed cable creation not generating a cable trace (CablePath). Cable creation now assigns terminations via NetBox's Cable.a_terminations/b_terminations model API and calls full_clean() before save(), instead of creating CableTermination rows directly — matching NetBox's own object-creation pattern and ensuring NetBox's internal trace_paths signal fires so cable paths are built correctly.
  • Cables created or deleted through the patcher now record "Modified by Cable Patcher Plugin" as the changelog message, so these changes are clearly distinguishable from changes made elsewhere in NetBox.
  • Location and Rack filters now support selecting multiple values at once; Site remains single-select. Selecting racks takes precedence over locations, which takes precedence over site.
  • Fixed low-contrast "Connected"/"Available" badge text in the port hover tooltip by using Bootstrap's text-bg-* helper classes instead of bg-*
  • api/devices/ and api/cables/ now accept repeated rack and location query params (e.g. ?rack=1&rack=2) for multi-value filtering

• Front port and rear port rendering in network mode (ports now visible alongside interfaces)
  • Module bay visualization: device cards show module bays as outlined sections with bay name and installed module type
  • Module bay population: install modules from the patcher UI with a searchable module type picker
  • Module uninstall: remove modules from bays directly in the patcher UI
  • Ports are grouped by module bay in the device card — base device ports appear first, then each module bay section
  • Empty module bays show a clickable placeholder to install a module
  • New API endpoints: api/module-types/ (search), api/module-bays/{id}/install/, api/module-bays/{id}/uninstall/
  • Port serializer now includes module_bay_id for module bay grouping

• Color-coded cables by type and status (planned, decommissioning)
  • Cable defaults bar with type, color, label, and quick-patch toggle
  • URL state persistence for site, location, rack, mode, and device selections
  • Front port and rear port backend support (serialization, compatibility rules, cable CRUD)
  • Console port and console server port support
  • Power port and power outlet support with dedicated mode
  • Network / Power / Console mode switching
  • Device drag-to-reorder within columns
  • Keyboard shortcuts (Escape, Delete, Enter)
  • Multi-select cables with Ctrl/Cmd+click
  • Floating cable info panel with cable details and delete action
  • Cable stub arrows for off-canvas or same-side connections
  • Dark mode support
  • Permission-based access control for cable operations
• First release on PyPI.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little bit helps, and credit will always be given.

We love your input! We want to make contributing to this project as easy and transparent as possible, whether it's:

  • Reporting a bug
  • Discussing the current state of the code
  • Submitting a fix
  • Proposing new features
  • Becoming a maintainer

docs.title: General Tips for Working on GitHub
docs.text:
• Register for a free GitHub account if you haven't already.
  • You can use GitHub Markdown for formatting text and adding images.
  • To help mitigate notification spam, please avoid "bumping" issues with no activity. (To vote an issue up or down, use a or reaction.)
  • Please avoid pinging members with @ unless they've previously expressed interest or involvement with that particular issue.
  • Familiarize yourself with this list of discussion anti-patterns and make every effort to avoid them.

docs.title: Report Bugs
docs.text:
Report bugs at https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher/issues.

If you are reporting a bug, please include:

  • Your operating system name and version.
  • Any details about your local setup that might be helpful in troubleshooting.
  • Detailed steps to reproduce the bug.

docs.title: Fix Bugs
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for bugs. Anything tagged with "bug" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

docs.title: Implement Features
docs.text: Look through the GitHub issues for features. Anything tagged with "enhancement" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

docs.title: Write Documentation
docs.text: NetBox Cable Patcher could always use more documentation, whether as part of the official NetBox Cable Patcher docs, in docstrings, or even on the web in blog posts, articles, and such.

docs.title: Submit Feedback
docs.text:
The best way to send feedback is to file an issue at https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher/issues.

If you are proposing a feature:

  • Explain in detail how it would work.
  • Keep the scope as narrow as possible, to make it easier to implement.
  • Remember that this is a volunteer-driven project, and that contributions are welcome :)

docs.title: Get Started!
docs.text:
Ready to contribute? Here's how to set up netbox-cable-patcher for local development.

  1. Fork the netbox-cable-patcher repo on GitHub.

  2. Clone your fork locally

    $ git clone git@github.com:your_name_here/netbox-cable-patcher.git

  3. Activate the NetBox virtual environment (see the NetBox documentation under Setting up a Development Environment):

    $ source ~/.venv/netbox/bin/activate

  4. Add the plugin to NetBox virtual environment in Develop mode (see Plugins Development):

    To ease development, it is recommended to go ahead and install the plugin at this point using setuptools' develop mode. This will create symbolic links within your Python environment to the plugin development directory. Call setup.py from the plugin's root directory with the develop argument (instead of install):

    $ python setup.py develop

  5. Create a branch for local development:

    $ git checkout -b name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature

    Now you can make your changes locally.

  6. Commit your changes and push your branch to GitHub:

    $ git add .
$ git commit -m "Your detailed description of your changes."
$ git push origin name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature

  7. Submit a pull request through the GitHub website.

docs.title: Pull Request Guidelines
docs.text:
Before you submit a pull request, check that it meets these guidelines:

  1. The pull request should include tests.
  2. If the pull request adds functionality, the docs should be updated. Put your new functionality into a function with a docstring, and add the feature to the list in README.md.
  3. The pull request should work for Python 3.13. Check https://github.com/joeladria/netbox-cable-patcher/actions and make sure that the tests pass for all supported Python versions.

docs.title: Deploying
docs.text: A reminder for the maintainers on how to deploy. Make sure all your changes are committed (including an entry in CHANGELOG.md) and that all tests pass. Then in the github project go to Releases and create a new release with a new tag. This will automatically upload the release to pypi:
